title: Collapse, Not Invariance: Diagnosing Auxiliary Objectives in Speech Anti-Spoofing

paper.title:
Collapse, Not Invariance: Diagnosing Auxiliary Objectives
in Speech Anti-Spoofing
paper.abstract:
Abstract Speech anti-spoofing countermeasures degrade when the generator, codec or
channel changes, and a common remedy is an auxiliary objective that shapes the
embedding space; whether it does is invisible to EER, a pure ranking metric.
We compare seven such objectives with cross-entropy over 113 113 runs on five
corpora, AASIST3 at three seeds plus four pre-trained detectors, and measure
the embedding space of the 24 24 AASIST3 runs directly. Raw augmentation
displacement makes cosine consistency look effective, but the gain is a
smaller space, not a more stable one: normalised by the spread, no
configuration consistently improves on cross-entropy. Every trained space is
dominated by the single decision axis expected for two classes, whose
training-set structure does not transfer, and four runs collapse to a
near-constant output that displacement rewards and EER reports as poor
accuracy. No auxiliary objective keeps an advantage over cross-entropy across
architectures, corpora and seeds.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Neural speech synthesis now produces speech hard to tell from genuine recordings, and countermeasures near-perfect in domain lose most of their accuracy once the generator, codec or channel changes [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] . A common response, on top of a self-supervised front-end [ 4 , 5 ] , is an auxiliary term on the embedding space , on the assumption that a better-structured representation transfers more readily [ 6 , 7 , 8 ] . These terms fall into four families: consistency regularisation pulls augmented views of an utterance together [ 9 ] , contrastive learning also pushes other utterances apart [ 10 ] , adversarial unlearning strips nuisance information [ 11 ] , and label smoothing , which adds no term on the embedding but is known to compress the penultimate geometry [ 12 ] , serves as a classifier-side control. Margin and one-class objectives, OC-Softmax [ 13 ] and SAMO [ 14 ] , and augmentation alone [ 15 ] are further routes to which the diagnostics below apply unchanged. All rest on the premise that such a term shapes the space as intended and that this structure is what transfers. EER cannot establish this: it depends only on the score ranking, so it cannot tell a space shaped as intended from one that was not, nor a collapsed encoder from a trained one that merely performs poorly. We read the detector’s internals instead, as [ 16 ] does for the branches of AASIST3. Each objective is also typically reported on its own architecture and corpus, often from a single run, a practice known to overstate differences between systems [ 17 ] . We compare seven auxiliary configurations with cross-entropy under one protocol: AASIST3 at three seeds and four pre-trained detectors of different design in three adaptation modes, 113 113 runs evaluated on five corpora, with the embedding space of the 24 24 AASIST3 runs measured directly. Our contributions are: • A scale-aware protocol for embedding objectives. Raw displacement A A changes under a rescaling that leaves the scores fixed, so we read it against the spread S S between utterances, confirm a vanishing S S with scale-free class separation, plot at a shared scale, and report seed-paired differences from cross-entropy. • Under it, apparent invariance is shrinkage. The 39 % 39\% lower displacement of cosine consistency is a 42 % 42\% smaller space; normalised, no objective is more invariant than cross-entropy on every seed, and every trained run keeps the single decision axis cross-entropy produces for two classes [ 18 ] , whose training-set structure does not carry to evaluation data. • EER hides two failures the protocol exposes. Four of 24 24 runs, from three objectives including one with no term on the embedding, collapse to a near-constant encoder that EER reports as poor accuracy and t-SNE draws as a healthy cloud; and single-seed rankings reverse: MSE beats cross-entropy by 12 % 12\% at one seed and trails every run at another.

sections.heading: 2.2 Data, training and evaluation
sections.text: Within each backbone every run uses identical settings, and no score normalisation or calibration is applied. 1) Data: Training uses the ASVspoof 5 train split [ 21 ] , validated on its dev split. Evaluation covers ASVspoof 5 eval (ASV5), the only in-domain condition, and four corpora disjoint from training: the ASVspoof 2021 DeepFake track (ASV21DF) [ 1 ] , In-the-Wild (ITW) [ 2 ] , VoiceWukong (VW) [ 22 ] and RuASD [ 23 ] . 2) Pre-processing: Audio is resampled to 16 16 kHz, cropped at a random offset or tiled to 64,600 64{,}600 samples ( ≈ 4.04 \approx 4.04 s) and pre-emphasised. 3) Augmentation: Every augmented view, diagnostics included, comes from one torch-audiomentations pipeline: gain ( p = 0.5 p{=}0.5 , [ − 10 , + 6 ] [-10,+6] dB), coloured noise ( 0.4 0.4 , SNR [ 10 , 40 ] [10,40] dB), polarity inversion ( 0.3 0.3 ), low-pass ( 0.3 0.3 , [ 4 , 7.5 ] [4,7.5] kHz), high-pass ( 0.3 0.3 , [ 80,400 ] [80,400] Hz), band-pass ( 0.2 0.2 , [ 0.4 , 3.5 ] [0.4,3.5] kHz) and band-stop ( 0.2 0.2 , [ 0.2 , 4 ] [0.2,4] kHz) filtering, time shift ( 0.4 0.4 , ± 10 % \pm 10\% ) and pitch shift ( 0.25 0.25 , ± 2 \pm 2 semitones). 4) Training AASIST3: AdamW, η = 10 − 4 \eta=10^{-4} , cosine annealing to 10 − 6 10^{-6} , effective batch 48 48 , 4 4 epochs in bf16 , the whole model trained end to end, each of the eight configurations at seeds 1 1 , 2 2 and 3 3 . The budget is fixed; Section 4.2 shows the training classes already separated at it, so evaluation EER reflects unseen attacks and codecs, not an unfitted model. 5) Fine-tuning existing detectors: The same objectives are applied to DF-Arena-500M [ 24 ] (DF-Arena below), XLSR-SLS [ 25 ] , Res2TCN [ 26 ] and WhisperMFCC+MesoNet [ 27 ] (WhisperMFCC below), each with its published schedule and the backbone at 0.1 × 0.1\times the head learning rate ( 4 4 epochs at 10 − 4 10^{-4} for Res2TCN and WhisperMFCC, 4 4 at 5 × 10 − 5 5\times 10^{-5} for XLSR-SLS, 2 2 at 5 × 10 − 5 5\times 10^{-5} for DF-Arena), in three modes: full, LoRA [ 28 ] ( r = 8 r{=}8 , 4 4 on WhisperMFCC) and head-only, which trains the head, the projector h h and any discriminator, so the auxiliary term acts on trainable layers in every mode. In all, 89 89 single-seed runs: the 88 88 entries of Table 3 and one repeated CE run. Its level, a mean over five corpora, is not comparable to published in-domain EERs. 6) Metrics: Each run keeps the epoch with the best dev EER. EER is computed on the pooled scores of each corpus, and the five-corpus mean averages the five, in-domain ASV5 included; AASIST3 EER is averaged over seeds unless a seed is named. RuASD is near chance for every AASIST3 run and contributes no order. Scores that are constant or vary only by numerical noise have no operating point, so their EER is reported as chance, 0.500 0.500 (three DF-Arena runs).

sections.heading: 4.1 Apparent invariance is shrinkage
sections.text: Judged by raw displacement, the quantity usually reported, cosine consistency appears to work: cosine averages A = 1.72 A=1.72 over seeds against 2.81 2.81 for CE , 39 % 39\% less. The spread explains the gain. The same runs average S = 2.94 S=2.94 against 5.10 5.10 , a space 42 % 42\% smaller, and the reduction in A A follows the reduction in S S seed by seed: on seed 2, where S S is unchanged ( 3.23 3.23 against 3.27 3.27 ), A A is unchanged too ( 1.78 1.78 against 1.90 1.90 ), and on seeds 1 and 3 both fall together. The seed-matched difference in R R between cosine and CE is + 0.08 +0.08 , − 0.03 -0.03 and + 0.04 +0.04 , no consistent reduction. Nothing fixes the scale of z z (Section 3 ), so A A reports shrinkage as invariance, and tuning α \alpha would change how far the space shrinks, not this. Across Table 1 , no objective is shown to be more invariant than cross-entropy: matched by seed, the difference from CE in R R changes sign, or lies within 0.01 0.01 of zero, for every objective with at least two trained seeds, for MSE − 0.01 -0.01 , + 0.03 +0.03 and − 0.11 -0.11 and for NT-Xent + 0.29 +0.29 , − 0.13 -0.13 and − 0.21 -0.21 . Effects smaller than the seed spread of R R ( 0.06 0.06 – 0.19 0.19 ) cannot be excluded with three seeds. Silhouette agrees: NT-Xent separates the classes less than CE on two of three seeds.

sections.heading: 4.2 One decision axis in every run, and four collapses
sections.text: Every trained space, CE included, is close to a single direction. In all 20 20 trained runs the first principal component holds 0.63 0.63 to 0.97 0.97 of the evaluation variance and lies along the difference of the class means ( | cos | ≥ 0.94 |\cos|\geq 0.94 ). For two classes this is the geometry cross-entropy is expected to produce [ 18 ] ; the finding is that no auxiliary term alters it: each acts through h h or a discriminator, and none constrains the covariance of z z as VICReg does [ 30 ] . On 600 600 training utterances the same runs approach neural collapse, with within-class variance 0.01 0.01 to 0.57 0.57 times the between-class variance and silhouette 0.57 0.57 to 0.94 0.94 , so they are not under-fitted to their training classes. As in image classification [ 31 ] , this structure does not transfer: on evaluation utterances within-class variance exceeds between-class variance 3.8 3.8 to 16.5 16.5 times, and the low evaluation silhouette tracks how far the classes overlap along that axis (Spearman ρ = 0.94 \rho=0.94 with the separation along it), not how one-dimensional the space is ( ρ = 0.08 \rho=0.08 with the PC1 fraction). Four runs go further: their spread vanishes (PC1 fraction 0.48 0.48 – 0.79 0.79 , overlapping the trained range). In these four runs S S lies between 0.01 0.01 and 0.17 0.17 , in the other 20 20 between 1.85 1.85 and 13.82 13.82 , with no run in the gap. They come from three objectives ( MAE at two seeds, smooth and DANN at one), and another seed of each trained normally. Since smooth adds no term on z z , no auxiliary term is needed for collapse: it is a failure of the training recipe that neither the supervised term nor, where present, SimSiam’s stop-gradient and predictor [ 9 ] avert, and that EER does not reveal. Three of the four collapses occur at seed 3, also the weakest CE seed (silhouette 0.107 0.107 ), so the trigger is as plausibly the seed’s trajectory as the objective. They are not rescaled healthy encoders: silhouette, Fisher ratio and the probe are invariant to a constant rescaling, yet the flagged runs fall below every trained run in silhouette ( 0.002 0.002 – 0.011 0.011 against ≥ 0.057 \geq 0.057 ) and Fisher ratio ( 0.8 0.8 – 2.6 2.6 against ≥ 3.9 \geq 3.9 ). Collapse is severe, not total: the probe still finds weak class information (AUC 0.65 0.65 – 0.67 0.67 ). A A , R R and EER miss it: A A ranks these runs the most invariant in the study, their R R stays within the 0.40 0.40 – 0.75 0.75 of trained runs, and their five-corpus mean EER of 0.48 0.48 – 0.53 0.53 looks like ordinary under-performance. Indeed the trained MSE run at seed 2 scores 0.575 0.575 , worse than any collapsed run, and MAE , collapsed at two of three seeds, has the lowest RuASD EER in Table 2 , where every objective lies between 0.47 0.47 and 0.51 0.51 . Figure 1 shows a collapsed run as a single point at a shared PCA scale, which t-SNE, the usual view, hides. What raw displacement rewards is thus a small space: the four collapsed runs at the extreme, and short of it the cosine runs, the smallest trained spaces. On DF-Arena three adversarial runs collapse as well ( GRL full, DANN full and LoRA): their encoder output varies by only 3 3 – 6 × 10 − 4 6\times 10^{-4} between utterances or not at all, DANN emitting one score for every input, so Table 3 reports them at chance rather than the tie order of noise.

sections.heading: 4.3 Rankings do not survive a change of seed or architecture
sections.text: A single seed can reverse a ranking. At seed 1 MSE reads 0.307 0.307 five-corpus mean EER against 0.349 0.349 for CE , a 12 % 12\% gain a single-run protocol would publish; seed 2 gives 0.575 0.575 , the worst of the 24 24 AASIST3 runs. Since MSE at this weight is a near-replicate of CE (Section 2.1 ), the two numbers bound the seed variance of the recipe, and the 0.002 0.002 agreement of the three CE seeds is a draw. In Table 2 the median over objectives of the seed standard deviation, 0.064 0.064 to 0.117 0.117 per corpus, exceeds the standard deviation of the eight objective means, 0.013 0.013 to 0.056 0.056 : seeds move EER more than objectives do. Matched by seed, none has a lower five-corpus mean than CE on all three seeds, and cosine , GRL and DANN are higher on every seed. Table 3 is single-seed and cannot rank objectives; it answers only whether any objective wins everywhere, and none does: under full fine-tuning the column minimum is CE on two architectures and smooth on the other two (tied with MSE on DF-Arena), and DANN is second on Res2TCN and, collapsed, last on DF-Arena. A repeated CE head-only run on Res2TCN differs by 0.011 0.011 , a lower bound on run-to-run variation since head-only trains the fewest parameters; within that floor the first two objectives are tied in 6 6 of the 11 11 columns, and within twice it in 9 9 . Head-only adaptation narrows the range relative to full fine-tuning on every architecture, from 0.125 0.125 to 0.008 0.008 on DF-Arena, but does not remove it: head-only smooth is 0.133 0.133 below CE on XLSR-SLS and cosine 0.045 0.045 below it on WhisperMFCC, candidate effects that need replication.

sections.heading: 5 Discussion and Conclusion
sections.text: Limitations. All runs train on ASVspoof 5 for at most four epochs with untuned weights of 0.01 0.01 – 0.02 0.02 ; longer schedules, which bring AASIST-family detectors with an SSL front-end far lower in-domain EER on ASVspoof 5 [ 5 ] , and larger weights are untested. Only AASIST3 is repeated, and three seeds show that rankings reverse without estimating variance or separating seed from objective as the collapse trigger. Diagnostics cover AASIST3 in domain and the adversarial DF-Arena runs only, against the training augmentations only; label-aware objectives (OC-Softmax, SAMO [ 13 , 14 ] ) are not covered. A detection metric and a single run cannot tell a shaped space from a shrunken or collapsed one; under the protocol above no tested objective beats cross-entropy across seed, architecture and corpus.

We compare seven such objectives with cross-entropy over 113 113 runs on five corpora, AASIST3 at three seeds plus four pre-trained detectors, and measure the embedding space of the 24 24 AASIST3 runs directly. Raw augmentation displacement makes cosine consistency look effective, but the gain is a smaller space, not a more stable one: normalised by the spread, no configuration consistently improves on cross-entropy. Every trained space is dominated by the single decision axis expected for two classes, whose training-set structure does not transfer, and four runs collapse to a near-constant output that displacement rewards and EER reports as poor accuracy. No auxiliary objective keeps an advantage over cross-entropy across architectures, corpora and seeds. Index Terms: anti-spoofing, speech deepfake detection, representation learning, representation collapse, cross-dataset generalisation † † address: 1 Lab260, Yerevan, Armenia 2 BitmanagerAI, Dubai, UAE 3 MTUCI, Moscow, Russia kborodin.research@gmail.com 1 Introduction Neural speech synthesis now produces speech hard to tell from genuine recordings, and countermeasures near-perfect in domain lose most of their accuracy once the generator, codec or channel changes [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] . A common response, on top of a self-supervised front-end [ 4 , 5 ] , is an auxiliary term on the embedding space , on the assumption that a better-structured representation transfers more readily [ 6 , 7 , 8 ] . These terms fall into four families: consistency regularisation pulls augmented views of an utterance together [ 9 ] , contrastive learning also pushes other utterances apart [ 10 ] , adversarial unlearning strips nuisance information [ 11 ] , and label smoothing , which adds no term on the embedding but is known to compress the penultimate geometry [ 12 ] , serves as a classifier-side control. Margin and one-class objectives, OC-Softmax [ 13 ] and SAMO [ 14 ] , and augmentation alone [ 15 ] are further routes to which the diagnostics below apply unchanged. All rest on the premise that such a term shapes the space as intended and that this structure is what transfers. EER cannot establish this: it depends only on the score ranking, so it cannot tell a space shaped as intended from one that was not, nor a collapsed encoder from a trained one that merely performs poorly. We read the detector’s internals instead, as [ 16 ] does for the branches of AASIST3. Each objective is also typically reported on its own architecture and corpus, often from a single run, a practice known to overstate differences between systems [ 17 ] . We compare seven auxiliary configurations with cross-entropy under one protocol: AASIST3 at three seeds and four pre-trained detectors of different design in three adaptation modes, 113 113 runs evaluated on five corpora, with the embedding space of the 24 24 AASIST3 runs measured directly. Our contributions are: • A scale-aware protocol for embedding objectives. Raw displacement A A changes under a rescaling that leaves the scores fixed, so we read it against the spread S S between utterances, confirm a vanishing S S with scale-free class separation, plot at a shared scale, and report seed-paired differences from cross-entropy. • Under it, apparent invariance is shrinkage. The 39 % 39\% lower displacement of cosine consistency is a 42 % 42\% smaller space; normalised, no objective is more invariant than cross-entropy on every seed, and every trained run keeps the single decision axis cross-entropy produces for two classes [ 18 ] , whose training-set structure does not carry to evaluation data. • EER hides two failures the protocol exposes. Four of 24 24 runs, from three objectives including one with no term on the embedding, collapse to a near-constant encoder that EER reports as poor accuracy and t-SNE draws as a healthy cloud; and single-seed rankings reverse: MSE beats cross-entropy by 12 % 12\% at one seed and trails every run at another. 2 Objectives and Experimental Setup 2.1 Auxiliary objectives The primary backbone is the AASIST3 architecture [ 19 ] , trained on ASVspoof 5 from a pre-trained wav2vec 2.0 XLSR-53 front-end [ 20 ] . Normalising z z removes c c but discards how small the space has become; kept in S S , a collapsed run lies 10 10 – 1000 × 1000\times below the rest, the role of VICReg’s variance term [ 30 ] . We call a run collapsed when S S falls more than an order of magnitude below every trained run; its output is near-constant, not constant. A healthy encoder multiplied by a small constant also has a vanishing S S , so S S only flags candidates; the scale-free silhouette and Fisher ratio then decide, since a rescaled encoder keeps both and a collapsed one loses them. The spread explains the gain. The same runs average S = 2.94 S=2.94 against 5.10 5.10 , a space 42 % 42\% smaller, and the reduction in A A follows the reduction in S S seed by seed: on seed 2, where S S is unchanged ( 3.23 3.23 against 3.27 3.27 ), A A is unchanged too ( 1.78 1.78 against 1.90 1.90 ), and on seeds 1 and 3 both fall together. The seed-matched difference in R R between cosine and CE is + 0.08 +0.08 , − 0.03 -0.03 and + 0.04 +0.04 , no consistent reduction. Nothing fixes the scale of z z (Section 3 ), so A A reports shrinkage as invariance, and tuning α \alpha would change how far the space shrinks, not this. Across Table 1 , no objective is shown to be more invariant than cross-entropy: matched by seed, the difference from CE in R R changes sign, or lies within 0.01 0.01 of zero, for every objective with at least two trained seeds, for MSE − 0.01 -0.01 , + 0.03 +0.03 and − 0.11 -0.11 and for NT-Xent + 0.29 +0.29 , − 0.13 -0.13 and − 0.21 -0.21 . Effects smaller than the seed spread of R R ( 0.06 0.06 – 0.19 0.19 ) cannot be excluded with three seeds. Silhouette agrees: NT-Xent separates the classes less than CE on two of three seeds. 4.2 One decision axis in every run, and four collapses Every trained space, CE included, is close to a single direction. In all 20 20 trained runs the first principal component holds 0.63 0.63 to 0.97 0.97 of the evaluation variance and lies along the difference of the class means ( | cos | ≥ 0.94 |\cos|\geq 0.94 ). For two classes this is the geometry cross-entropy is expected to produce [ 18 ] ; the finding is that no auxiliary term alters it: each acts through h h or a discriminator, and none constrains the covariance of z z as VICReg does [ 30 ] . On 600 600 training utterances the same runs approach neural collapse, with within-class variance 0.01 0.01 to 0.57 0.57 times the between-class variance and silhouette 0.57 0.57 to 0.94 0.94 , so they are not under-fitted to their training classes. As in image classification [ 31 ] , this structure does not transfer: on evaluation utterances within-class variance exceeds between-class variance 3.8 3.8 to 16.5 16.5 times, and the low evaluation silhouette tracks how far the classes overlap along that axis (Spearman ρ = 0.94 \rho=0.94 with the separation along it), not how one-dimensional the space is ( ρ = 0.08 \rho=0.08 with the PC1 fraction). Four runs go further: their spread vanishes (PC1 fraction 0.48 0.48 – 0.79 0.79 , overlapping the trained range). In these four runs S S lies between 0.01 0.01 and 0.17 0.17 , in the other 20 20 between 1.85 1.85 and 13.82 13.82 , with no run in the gap. They come from three objectives ( MAE at two seeds, smooth and DANN at one), and another seed of each trained normally. Since smooth adds no term on z z , no auxiliary term is needed for collapse: it is a failure of the training recipe that neither the supervised term nor, where present, SimSiam’s stop-gradient and predictor [ 9 ] avert, and that EER does not reveal. Three of the four collapses occur at seed 3, also the weakest CE seed (silhouette 0.107 0.107 ), so the trigger is as plausibly the seed’s trajectory as the objective. They are not rescaled healthy encoders: silhouette, Fisher ratio and the probe are invariant to a constant rescaling, yet the flagged runs fall below every trained run in silhouette ( 0.002 0.002 – 0.011 0.011 against ≥ 0.057 \geq 0.057 ) and Fisher ratio ( 0.8 0.8 – 2.6 2.6 against ≥ 3.9 \geq 3.9 ). Collapse is severe, not total: the probe still finds weak class information (AUC 0.65 0.65 – 0.67 0.67 ). A A , R R and EER miss it: A A ranks these runs the most invariant in the study, their R R stays within the 0.40 0.40 – 0.75 0.75 of trained runs, and their five-corpus mean EER of 0.48 0.48 – 0.53 0.53 looks like ordinary under-performance. Indeed the trained MSE run at seed 2 scores 0.575 0.575 , worse than any collapsed run, and MAE , collapsed at two of three seeds, has the lowest RuASD EER in Table 2 , where every objective lies between 0.47 0.47 and 0.51 0.51 . Figure 1 shows a collapsed run as a single point at a shared PCA scale, which t-SNE, the usual view, hides. What raw displacement rewards is thus a small space: the four collapsed runs at the extreme, and short of it the cosine runs, the smallest trained spaces. On DF-Arena three adversarial runs collapse as well ( GRL full, DANN full and LoRA): their encoder output varies by only 3 3 – 6 × 10 − 4 6\times 10^{-4} between utterances or not at all, DANN emitting one score for every input, so Table 3 reports them at chance rather than the tie order of noise. 4.3 Rankings do not survive a change of seed or architecture A single seed can reverse a ranking. At seed 1 MSE reads 0.307 0.307 five-corpus mean EER against 0.349 0.349 for CE , a 12 % 12\% gain a single-run protocol would publish; seed 2 gives 0.575 0.575 , the worst of the 24 24 AASIST3 runs. Since MSE at this weight is a near-replicate of CE (Section 2.1 ), the two numbers bound the seed variance of the recipe, and the 0.002 0.002 agreement of the three CE seeds is a draw. In Table 2 the median over objectives of the seed standard deviation, 0.064 0.064 to 0.117 0.117 per corpus, exceeds the standard deviation of the eight objective means, 0.013 0.013 to 0.056 0.056 : seeds move EER more than objectives do. Matched by seed, none has a lower five-corpus mean than CE on all three seeds, and cosine , GRL and DANN are higher on every seed. Table 3 is single-seed and cannot rank objectives; it answers only whether any objective wins everywhere, and none does: under full fine-tuning the column minimum is CE on two architectures and smooth on the other two (tied with MSE on DF-Arena), and DANN is second on Res2TCN and, collapsed, last on DF-Arena. A repeated CE head-only run on Res2TCN differs by 0.011 0.011 , a lower bound on run-to-run variation since head-only trains the fewest parameters; within that floor the first two objectives are tied in 6 6 of the 11 11 columns, and within twice it in 9 9 . Head-only adaptation narrows the range relative to full fine-tuning on every architecture, from 0.125 0.125 to 0.008 0.008 on DF-Arena, but does not remove it: head-only smooth is 0.133 0.133 below CE on XLSR-SLS and cosine 0.045 0.045 below it on WhisperMFCC, candidate effects that need replication. 5 Discussion and Conclusion Limitations. All runs train on ASVspoof 5 for at most four epochs with untuned weights of 0.01 0.01 – 0.02 0.02 ; longer schedules, which bring AASIST-family detectors with an SSL front-end far lower in-domain EER on ASVspoof 5 [ 5 ] , and larger weights are untested. Only AASIST3 is repeated, and three seeds show that rankings reverse without estimating variance or separating seed from objective as the collapse trigger. Diagnostics cover AASIST3 in domain and the adversarial DF-Arena runs only, against the training augmentations only; label-aware objectives (OC-Softmax, SAMO [ 13 , 14 ] ) are not covered.
